item.description: El 18 de septiembre, Dmitry, un moscovita de 35 años que trabaja en publicidad, votó en las falsas elecciones parlamentarias de Rusia. Escribió la palabra «criminal» en su papeleta, la introdujo en la urna y se dirigió directamente al aeropuerto, donde tomó un vuelo a Estambul. Fue uno de los miles que se han marchado en las últimas semanas, por temor a que el «procedimiento electoral especial» —como algunos rusos han empezado a llamar a sus elecciones— allanara el camino para una nueva ola de movilización militar.Cuando Vladímir Putin declaró una movilización parcial en septiembre de 2022… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.

item.title: France: Far right leader Marine Le Pen gains popularity amid nationwide riots
item.description: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met with union leaders today in France. His government admitted law enforcement officers had lost control this past weekend during protests which resulted in scenes of violence and looting. The country is bracing for more protests – the Yellow Vest movement called on demonstrators to take to the street on Saturday. As the events unfold, far-right leader Marine Le Pen is gaining popularity. Details and analysis by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: Measures would remove some penalties for those helping women access abortion but are ‘small-scale step’, say campaigners Poland’s lower house of parliament has approved two bills aimed at loosening a near-total ban on abortions, in what campaigners have described as a “small-scale step” ahead of protests calling on the government to fulfil its promises to overhaul the country’s laws. The new measures, which are likely to be vetoed by Poland’s nationalist president, would remove some of the criminal penalties for those who help women to access abortion care and allow terminations in cases of… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.description: President Donald Trump’s administration has ⁠revoked over 300,000 ⁠US visas during his second ⁠term, the State Department said on Tuesday as the federal government continues its sweeping immigration crackdown. In an update ‌issued on August 10, the State Department had put the number of visa revocations since Trump’s current term began in January 2025 at over 175,000.
